findings.where: Article specimen: the article title 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law', against the type-pair note and every other heading on the tile (MARK M. MOSELEY, OVERPASS, CUT · MEASURED · EXACT)
findings.fault: The type-pair note says headings are set in ExtraBold tracked capitals. The one heading on the article page, the page Angélique will repeat most, is set in bold mixed case with no tracking. The tile states a heading style and then breaks it on its own article.
findings.who_objects: The layout-round designer and Angélique, who add posts. They can't tell from the tile which style a post title takes, so article titles will drift between the two.

findings.where: Dates and measures across the page: the article byline '18 September 2024' in proportional sans next to the lecture card's '2026-04-23' in mono; 'SCALE NTS' in the hero subtitle and the 'NTS' and 'EQ' dimension labels in the drawing in tracked sans, while the title block's 'NTS' and the drawing's '±0.00' are in mono
findings.fault: The tile's own rule is mono for measurement only: drawing numbers, levels, dates and scales. Like items are still set unlike. One article date is in sans and written out, the other is in mono and in ISO form. The scale 'NTS' is mono in the title block but sans in the hero and on the drawing. The lecture line also mixes two separators ('•' and '·').
findings.who_objects: A careful reader on an article page sees two dates of the same kind set two ways, which looks unedited. The layout round inherits no clear rule for when the mono voice applies.

findings.where: Hero, the two-line subtitle under MARK M. MOSELEY ('INFRASTRUCTURE ADVISOR / LONGITUDINAL SECTION A-A • SCALE NTS')
findings.fault: Mark's role, the one fact a visitor needs beside his name, has the same small tracked caps, size, weight and colour as the drawing's jargon line under it. Nothing in the type ranks 'Infrastructure advisor' above 'Longitudinal section A-A'. On the phone the subtitle wraps so that the '•' hangs at a line end and 'SCALE NTS' drops to a third line.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer scanning the first screen for who this man is and what he does. The role reads as part of the drawing label, not as his job.

findings.where: Section labels against the item labels inside them: PALETTE, TEXTURE, TYPE PAIR, AN ARTICLE PAGE and MOTION SKETCH against DIAZO BLUE, LINEWORK, EARTH HATCH, POCHE and the table heads ELEMENT, START, LENGTH, EASING
findings.fault: Section headings and the labels inside them are set alike: small bold capitals with wide tracking, at about the same size and colour. Only the rule under the section label tells the two ranks apart. With the nav, the button, REPLAY THE CUT and the subtitle also in tracked caps, the spaced-capital style marks too many levels to rank any of them.
findings.who_objects: The layout-round designer, who takes this tile's label system into the site's section heads, eyebrows and nav. They get one capital style for three or four ranks.

findings.where: Small reversed notes in Overpass Light: the palette swatch notes, the texture caption, the type-pair notes and the motion-sketch notes ('Total 1100 ms…'), on desktop and phone
findings.fault: The small supporting text is set in the Light weight, reversed out of mid blue, with the grid lines running through it. At about 13–14 px the thin strokes look faint and broken compared with the Regular body text. This is the weight the tile offers for captions and metadata.
findings.who_objects: An older bank reader of an article's captions or meta lines, which will inherit this setting. Thin reversed text over a grid is tiring to read even where it passes the contrast check.
